candidates.label: Ovarian malignant mixed germ cell tumor (yolk sac tumor and choriocarcinoma) with brain metastasis to third ventricle/hypothalamic region, presenting with seizures and elevated tumor markers
missing_or_uncertain: Ovarian mass not visualized on ultrasound; histologic confirmation needed

candidates.label: Primary intracranial non-germinomatous germ cell tumor (yolk sac tumor/choriocarcinoma) with obstructive hydrocephalus and seizures, with secondary β-hCG effect on uterus
missing_or_uncertain: Pelvic findings atypical for primary intracranial tumor; need CSF markers and biopsy

candidates.label: Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (choriocarcinoma) with brain metastasis, but AFP elevation atypical
missing_or_uncertain: AFP elevation not typical; need histology and hCG fractionation

candidates.label: Ovarian immature teratoma with brain metastasis and elevated AFP/β-hCG
missing_or_uncertain: CA-125 elevation more common in epithelial tumors; teratoma less likely to cause such high β-hCG

candidates.label: Hypothalamic hamartoma with gelastic seizures and incidental elevated tumor markers
missing_or_uncertain: Seizures are generalized tonic-clonic, not gelastic; tumor markers unexplained

response.rationale: The combination of markedly elevated β-hCG and AFP, along with an enlarged uterus and non-visualized ovaries, strongly suggests an ovarian malignant mixed germ cell tumor (yolk sac tumor and choriocarcinoma). The third ventricle lesion with ventriculomegaly and seizures is best explained as a brain metastasis. Primary intracranial germ cell tumor is less likely given the pelvic findings, though it remains a differential. Other options (gestational trophoblastic neoplasia, teratoma, hamartoma) are less consistent with the full marker profile and clinical presentation.
